title: 2_Compound Angle Identities

findings.finding: The opening worked examples substitute exact trigonometric ratios without an opening review rehearsing their recall.
findings.breakdown: Students must recall the ratios for 30°, 45° and 90° to follow the worked substitutions. The compound-angle formula block does not supply them.
findings.checked: Searched all supplied teaching. No opening review rehearses exact ratios. Removed reference-triangle construction and signed-ratio recovery from this finding because p4-worked explicitly demonstrates those steps as part of this topic's method.
findings.assumptions: Exact-ratio recall is prior knowledge from the listed trigonometry booklets. Decimal calculator evaluation does not supply the required exact forms.

repair.proposal: Before p3-identities-block, add three short items: (a) State sin30° and cos30°. Answers: 1/2 and √3/2. (b) State sin45° and cos45°. Answers: 1/√2 and 1/√2. (c) State sin90° and cos90°. Answers: 1 and 0. Keep the review within one page.

findings.doneWhen: The review rehearses the exact ratios substituted in the opening worked examples.

findings.finding: Four later practice tasks repeat complete earlier tasks without an explicit retrieval or comparison purpose.
findings.breakdown: Each later copy repeats the same expression, values and required operation, allowing the earlier working and result to be reproduced unchanged.
findings.checked: Compared all four complete pairs, including their enclosing instructions. Each pair requires the same whole task; no diagrams or additional givens distinguish them. Different equivalent answer forms do not distinguish the tasks. No explicit repetition purpose is supplied.
findings.assumptions: Each independently answerable part is a whole task. The three p7-q8 parts have no shared givens requiring their angles to remain identical.

repair.proposal: Replace p5-q3-a with “Prove sin(180° + A) = −sin A.” Expected working: 0cos A − sin A = −sin A. Replace p6-q4-b with “Prove 2cos(θ + π/6) = √3cosθ − sinθ.” Expected working: 2[(√3/2)cosθ − (1/2)sinθ] = √3cosθ − sinθ. Replace p7-q8-a with “Find sin165° in exact form.” Answer: (√3 − 1)/(2√2). Replace p7-q8-b with “Find cos165° in exact form.” Answer: −(√3 + 1)/(2√2).

findings.doneWhen: Each later copy uses different values while retaining its original task structure, with the corresponding answer supplied.

findings.finding: Add a matched comparison of the signs in sine and cosine expansions.
findings.breakdown: Holding the angle expressions fixed makes the matching sign for sine and reversed sign for cosine directly comparable.
findings.checked: The existing practice covers all four expansions but does not provide a matched run. All proposed expansions are correct and use the identities already supplied. Changed the angle pair to avoid repeating p5-q1-a.
findings.assumptions: The existing instruction to expand using compound-angle identities applies to the added parts.

repair.proposal: After p5-q1-f, add one instruction: “Predict the sign between the terms before expanding.” Add (g) sin(2x + y), answer sin2x cos y + cos2x sin y; (h) sin(2x − y), answer sin2x cos y − cos2x sin y; (i) cos(2x + y), answer cos2x cos y − sin2x sin y; (j) cos(2x − y), answer cos2x cos y + sin2x sin y. Follow with (k) cos(3u − 2v), answer cos3u cos2v + sin3u sin2v. The angle pair stays fixed through the run while the function and inner sign vary.

findings.doneWhen: The four matched expansions and one unpatterned follow-up appear under p5-q1.

findings.finding: The first double-angle proof combines squared-binomial expansion and the Pythagorean identity without reviewing either prerequisite.
findings.breakdown: Following the proof requires retaining the cross term and replacing sin²x + cos²x with 1. Neither step is rehearsed before their combined use.
findings.checked: Searched the supplied preceding teaching and practice. Compound-angle work rehearses expansion by trigonometric formulas, proof structure and reference triangles, but does not rehearse squared-binomial expansion or sin²x + cos²x = 1. The double-angle formula block uses the Pythagorean relationship without explaining or rehearsing it.
findings.assumptions: Both are substantial prior algebra and trigonometry skills taught elsewhere in the listed course. No calculator assumption is needed.

repair.proposal: Before p11-identities-block, add: (a) Expand (a + b)². Answer: a² + 2ab + b². (b) Complete sin²x + cos²x = __. Answer: 1. (c) Expand and simplify (sin x − cos x)² using part b. Answer: 1 − 2sin x cos x. Keep the review within one page.

findings.doneWhen: The review rehearses both prerequisite steps before their combined use in the worked proof.

findings.finding: Add matched quadrant variations to compare their effects on sine and cosine double-angle values.
findings.breakdown: Holding |sin x| fixed exposes how the signs of sin x and cos x affect sin2x while cos2x remains unchanged.
findings.checked: Existing p12-q3 has no matched quadrant run. Verified all five proposed answer pairs using sin2x = 2sin x cos x and cos2x = 1 − 2sin²x. Reference-triangle recovery and quadrant signs are demonstrated before this practice.
findings.assumptions: Each stated interval or acute/obtuse condition fixes the required signs.

repair.proposal: After p12-q3-d, add one instruction: “Predict which answers will stay the same before calculating.” Add (e) If sin x = 3/5 and x is acute, find sin2x and cos2x. Answers: 24/25, 7/25. (f) If sin x = 3/5 and x is obtuse, find sin2x and cos2x. Answers: −24/25, 7/25. (g) If sin x = −3/5 and π < x < 3π/2, find sin2x and cos2x. Answers: 24/25, 7/25. (h) If sin x = −3/5 and −π/2 < x < 0, find sin2x and cos2x. Answers: −24/25, 7/25. Follow with (i) If cos x = −5/13 and x is obtuse, find sin2x and cos2x. Answers: −120/169, −119/169. Through the matched run, |sin x| stays fixed and the quadrant changes.

findings.doneWhen: The matched quadrant run and unpatterned follow-up appear as further parts of p12-q3.

protectedGroups.observation: The sine identity doubles the whole angle expression.
protectedGroups.varies: The argument changes from x to 20 degrees to 3theta.
protectedGroups.invariant: The expression has the form 2sin u cos u.

protectedGroups.observation: The tangent identity applies equally to symbolic, numerical and multiplied arguments.
protectedGroups.varies: The argument changes from alpha to 70 degrees to 4x.
protectedGroups.invariant: The expression has the form 2tan u/(1-tan^2 u).

importReview: Lean content review table: 32 of 32 blocks passed.

dropped.reason: Defeated by the extension exclusion for a tangential distinction: the stated purpose is distinguishing a tangent value from a unique angle, rather than exposing a relationship central to compound-angle identities. The proposed answers are mathematically correct: the acute sum is 45°, and shifting α to quadrant III gives 225°.

candidates.finding: Use the existing tangent ratios to connect the calculated ratio with the possible angle sums.
